# Review finding (P0) — config.py / stats.py: default flip exposes latent empty-batch crash

- Date: 2026-10-18. Files: config.py (DETAILED_REPORT False -> True), stats.py:4, app.py:7-9, tests/test_report.py.
- Pattern: flipping a config default promotes a previously opt-in code path to the default path, but that path had a latent edge-case bug that was never tested. `summarize(values, detailed=True)` does `sum(values) / len(values)` with no empty guard, so `report([])` with the new default raises ZeroDivisionError. The README contract says empty batches are valid in either mode and yield `Items: 0`.
- The test suite covers only explicit plain empty (`detailed=False`) and populated defaults, so all 4 tests pass while the contract is broken.
- Fix: guard the mean (`if detailed and values:`) in stats.summarize; add tests for `report([])` default and `report([], detailed=True)` -> "Items: 0".
- Lesson: when changing a default, re-test the newly-default path against the edge cases (empty, zero, None) the old default handled.
